# The World's Oldest Living People in 2026
All of the oldest living people in 2026 are women.
Daniel Dimays Sumarno
Daniel Dimays Sumarno
July 30, 2026 5:00 PM GMT+7 · 1 min read

...

The world's oldest living people represent an extraordinary group of supercentenarians—individuals who have reached the age of 110 or beyond. Their lives span more than a century of history, encompassing world wars, technological revolutions, medical breakthroughs, and profound social change.
As of 2026, the ten oldest verified living people are all women, highlighting the well-documented trend that women generally outlive men. Their ages have been validated by organizations specializing in longevity research and record keeping.
At the top of the list is **Ethel Caterham** of the United Kingdom, born on **21 August 1909** . She is recognized as the world's oldest verified living person and has lived through more than 116 years of remarkable history, making her one of the oldest people ever documented.

...

The fourth oldest living person is **Yolanda Beltrão de Azevedo** of Brazil, born on **13 January 1911** . She is followed by **Shigeko Kagawa** of Japan, born on **28 May 1911** , and **Beatriz Ferreira Duarte** , also of Brazil, born on **21 June 1911** .

...

Rounding out the upper portion of the list are **Fuyo Kishimoto** of Japan, born on **20 December 1911** , **Ilse Meingast** , born on **14 March 1912** , **Madeleine Dellamonica** of France, born on **23 July 1912** , and **Angelica Tiscornia** , born on **22 August 1912** .
Each has surpassed 114 years of age, placing them among the oldest verified people alive in the world.

results.title: Oldest person ever | Guinness World Records
excerpts:
# Oldest person ever
What
122/164 year(s):day(s)
Where
France (Arles)
When
04 August 1997
The greatest fully authenticated age to which any human has ever lived is 122 years 164 days by Jeanne Louise Calment (France). Born on 21 February 1875 to Nicolas (1837 - 1931) and Marguerite (neé Gilles 1838 - 1924), Jeanne died at a nursing home in Arles, southern France on 4 August 1997.

...

[Jeanne](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2024/2/oldest-person-ever-122-year-old-jeanne-calments-extraordinary-life-765016) lived a quiet life, but an unprecedentedly long one.

...

Two years later, on 11 January 1988, she became the oldest living person; and two years after that, now aged 114, she appeared in a film about Van Gogh, _Vincent et moi_ (1990), as herself, thereby becoming the [oldest film actress](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/oldest-actress) ever.

...

Her tranquil state of mind probably contributed to Jeanne’s long, long life (“That’s why they call me Calment,” she quipped at her 121st birthday in 1996), and may have helped her stave off senility – she remained clear thinking right up to the day she passed away in 1997, aged 122 years 164 days.
Jeanne was also famous for her wit, and felt that her sense of humour also played its part in her remarkable longevity. At her 120th birthday, journalists asked her what kind of future she expected. “A very short one,” she replied.
In the video below we look back at the oldest people on record and explore the science behind old age. What makes some people live longer than others? And is it likely that anyone will beat the current record? Experts give us their take on the future of this record, and what makes humans live to a ripe old age.

## Ranked: The World’s Oldest People in History
### Key Takeaways
* The longest verified human lifespan belongs to **Jeanne Calment** of France, who lived 122 years and 164 days, significantly above the other records.
* Women are the leaders when it comes to extreme longevity, with all 10 oldest recorded people being female, while men’s maximum verified lifespans are several years shorter.

Third in this ranking is **Sarah Knauss** , the oldest person ever from the United States. Prior to her death, there were six living generations within her family. Staff members at the nursing home Sarah lived in remembered her for her calm temperament.

### The World’s Oldest Men in History
**Jiroemon Kimura** of Japan claims the title of the world’s oldest man, living 117 years, 54 days. He attributed his longevity to staying active and only eating until about 80% full (a Japanese concept known as _hara hachi bunme_ ).

### Why Do Women Live Longer Than Men?
Women typically [live longer than men](https://www.visualcapitalist.com/charted-american-life-expectancy-trends-2023/) for a mix of biological and behavioral reasons.
